title: You froze in that meeting today.
lines: You knew the answer. The words just didn't come.
That doesn't make you less smart.
It makes you human in a room that moved fast.
Next time, you get to say: let me come back to you on that.
end: Send this to someone who froze today.
cta: Have you ever frozen in a meeting?
hook: You froze in that meeting today. It's still replaying.
cast: a Black man in his 20s with short twists, in a gray crewneck
setting: sitting alone in his car in a parking garage after work, staring ahead
caption: You froze in that meeting today. 💬

says: We don't have budget for raises this year.
means: I need you to make the case for me.
I'm hoping you'll drop it.
say: I understand. What would it take to revisit this in 3 months?
Can we put the numbers I'm hitting in writing now?
If salary is fixed, can we talk title or extra time off?
cta: Has a boss ever told you there's no budget?
hook: You finally asked for the raise. And got the budget speech.
cast: a Black woman in her 30s with braids, in a mustard sweater
setting: a glass-walled meeting room, her manager across the table looking apologetic
caption: You finally asked for the raise. 💬

title: Stop saying these 3 things when you ask for a raise
pairs: I feel like I deserve more.
Here are the results I delivered this year.
Is there any way I could get a raise?
I'd like to discuss moving my pay to X.
I know it's a bad time, but...
Is now a good time to talk about my pay?
cta: Have you asked for a raise this year?
hook: You rehearsed it 20 times. Then said 'sorry' first.
cast: a Middle Eastern man in his 30s with dark wavy hair, in a light blue shirt
setting: standing outside his manager's office door, taking a breath
caption: You rehearsed it 20 times. 💬

means: I like you, but I'm testing your price.
I'll respect a confident answer.
say: Possibly. Cheaper compared to what?
What part of this matters most to you?
Money aside, is this the result you want?
cta: What's the lowest anyone has asked you to go?
hook: They loved your work. Then asked you to cut your price.
cast: a South Asian man in his 30s with a short beard, freelance designer in a denim shirt
setting: a sunny home office, video call with a client on his laptop
caption: They loved your work. 💬

title: You undercharged again.
lines: Pricing low felt safer than hearing no.
But every discount teaches them what you're worth.
Next time, ask what fixing this is worth to them first.
end: Send this to someone who undercharges.
cta: What would you charge if you weren't scared?
hook: You undercharged again. And you knew it as you said it.
cast: a white man in his 40s with a red beard, carpenter in a work apron
setting: his workshop, looking at an invoice on his phone with a sigh
caption: You undercharged again. 💬

means: Give me a number so I can anchor low.
I have a range I'm not telling you.
say: I'd love to hear the range budgeted for this role first.
Based on my research, roles like this pay between X and Y.
I'm flexible for the right fit. What's the full package?
cta: Do you name a number first, or make them go first?
hook: One question can cost you $10,000. Don't answer it first.
cast: an East Asian woman in her 20s with a sleek bob, in a navy blazer
setting: a cozy cafe, on a phone call with a recruiter, notebook open
caption: One question can cost you $10,000. 💬

title: Stop saying these 3 things in work emails
pairs: Sorry to bother you...
Following up on this.
Just checking in.
Can you confirm by Friday?
Does that make sense?
Let me know your questions.
cta: Which one do you catch yourself typing?
hook: One word in your emails makes you sound less sure.

setting: typing at a laptop in a bright modern office, coffee beside him
caption: One word in your emails makes you sound less sure. 💬

says: Can you just quickly help me with this?
means: I'm handing you my work.
I'm counting on you not saying no.
say: I can't today, but I can show you where to start.
Happy to after I finish mine. Does Thursday work?
Which of my tasks should I drop to take this on?
cta: Who's the coworker who always needs a quick favor?
hook: It's 4:55. And here comes the 'quick favor'.

title: Nobody tells you how lonely asking for money feels.
lines: Raises, rates, invoices. It always feels awkward.
You were taught being humble means staying quiet.
But asking is not greedy. It's how fair happens.
The people who ask get paid. Start asking.
end: Send this to someone who needs to hear it.
cta: Who taught you money talk was rude?
hook: Nobody tells you how lonely asking for money feels.
cast: a South Asian woman in her 30s with long dark hair, in a teal kurta top
setting: sitting by a rainy window at home with tea, laptop closed
caption: Nobody tells you how lonely asking for money feels. 💬

says: I need to think about it.
means: Something isn't clear or isn't worth it yet.
I don't want to say no to your face.
say: That makes sense. What's on your mind about it?
Is it the money, the timing, or something else?
Let's suppose that's solved. What would you want next?
cta: What's the hardest objection you hear?
hook: 'I need to think about it.' The sale is slipping away.

caption: 'I need to think about it. 💬

title: Stop saying these 3 things when you negotiate a price
pairs: What's your best price?
What flexibility do you have on this?
That's way too much.
That's above my budget. Help me see the value.
I'll take it.
If you include X, we have a deal.

hook: You paid full price again. Because of the first thing you said.

says: We need you to stay late tonight.
means: I didn't plan ahead, and you're the easy yes.
I assume your time is free.
say: I can stay until 6. What's the one thing that must be done?
I have a commitment tonight. I can start early tomorrow.
If this keeps happening, can we talk about workload?

hook: Dinner's waiting at home. And your boss says 'stay late'.

setting: an office at dusk, packing her bag as her boss stops at her desk
caption: Dinner's waiting at home. 💬

title: If you cried in your car before work today, read this.
lines: You're not weak. You're carrying a lot.
Some jobs take more than they give.
Your worth was never your job title.
Today you made it in. That counts.
end: Send this to someone having a hard work week.
cta: What got you through your worst work week?
hook: If you cried in your car before work today, read this.
cast: a white woman in her 20s with a messy blonde bun, in a nurse's scrubs

says: Sorry, payment will be a little late.
means: You're not my priority this week.
I'll keep pushing if you let me.
say: Thanks for telling me. What date can I expect it?
Per our agreement, a late fee applies after 7 days.
I'll pause new work until the invoice is paid.
cta: Longest you've ever waited to get paid?
hook: You did the work. Now you're chasing your own money.

title: Stop saying these 3 things when you say no
pairs: I'm so sorry, I just can't.
I can't take this on.
Maybe later?
Not this month. Ask me in January.
I'll try.
I won't be able to, but here's who can.

says: Do you have any questions for us?
means: Show me you're serious.
This is your last chance to stand out.
say: What would make someone great in this role in 90 days?
What's the biggest challenge your team faces right now?
Is there anything that makes you hesitate about me?

hook: The interview's ending. And your mind just went blank.

setting: an interview across a wooden table, two interviewers smiling politely
caption: The interview's ending. 💬

title: They gave the promotion to someone else.
lines: Smiling through it was the hardest work you did all year.
It's okay to be disappointed.
Ask them: what would have made it me?
Then decide if this place still deserves you.
end: Send this to someone who got passed over.
cta: Have you ever been passed over?
hook: They gave the promotion to someone else. You smiled anyway.
cast: an East Asian man in his 40s with short gray hair, in a white shirt and loosened tie
setting: clapping at an office celebration for a coworker, his smile not reaching his eyes
caption: They gave the promotion to someone else. 💬

says: Rent is going up next month.

say: I've paid on time every month. Can we keep the current rate?
Would you take a smaller increase for a longer lease?
I'm comparing places nearby. Is there room to talk?
cta: How much did your rent go up this year?
hook: The rent email came in. Your stomach dropped.

pairs: I'm a perfectionist.

Whatever you think is fair.
Based on the role, I'm looking for X.

hook: You nailed the interview. Then one answer gave it away.

means: I want to fix something before it grows.

say: Thank you. What's the one thing I should change first?
Can you share an example so I get it right?

hook: 'Can we talk?' And your heart starts racing.

title: Your parents never talked about money.
lines: No one taught you to negotiate, invoice, or say your price.

Gaps can be filled one script at a time.
end: Send this to someone learning money talk late.

hook: Your parents never talked about money. So you never learned how.
